Synopsis:
    Swiss parliamentary committee is proposing AT1/CoCo bond reform as an alternative to the government's stricter CET1 capital requirements for UBS. The committee favors a 50-50 CET1/AT1 split, with enhanced loss-absorption features and a higher effective trigger (~11% vs current ~7%). The article argues this approach is flawed: it creates an idiosyncratic Swiss regulatory regime that may raise investor costs, and a higher trigger point is unlikely to prevent failure — Credit Suisse collapsed with a CET1 ratio of 14%, far above its minimum. UBS estimates ~$13B in additional AT1 issuance, costing ~$1B/year, with ~1pp ROTE drag vs ~4pp under the government's harder-line plan.
